package_info.package_versions: versions vulnerable to CVE-2021-30116 (exact versions not specified in report)
package_info.why_malicious: The Kaseya VSA software was exploited via a zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2021-30116) that allowed unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary commands on managed endpoints. Attackers leveraged this to deploy ransomware at scale across downstream MSP customers, resulting in widespread business disruption.

execution_context.file_location: Kaseya VSA web interface (vulnerable endpoint exposed to internet)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Attackers exploited a pre-authentication remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability (CVE-2021-30116) to send specially crafted requests to the Kaseya VSA server, bypassing authentication and executing arbitrary commands on the server and managed endpoints.
malicious_snippets.code_language: unknown (exploit payload, likely shell or PowerShell commands delivered via HTTP)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code exploits a pre-auth RCE vulnerability to execute arbitrary commands on the Kaseya VSA server, which then propagates malicious payloads to managed endpoints, resulting in ransomware deployment.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Pre-authentication RCE allowing arbitrary command execution is a critical security risk, especially in remote management software.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior expects strict authentication and authorization before any command execution; this exploit bypasses all controls.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate remote management tools may execute commands on endpoints, but only after proper authentication and authorization.
key_indicators: Arbitrary command execution via network requests
Propagation of ransomware payloads to managed endpoints

execution_context.file_location: Managed endpoint (deployed via Kaseya VSA agent)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Ransomware payload delivered to endpoints via Kaseya VSA agent, encrypting files and displaying ransom note.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After exploitation, the code executes on managed endpoints, encrypts files, and displays a ransom note, resulting in business disruption and extortion.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Deployment of ransomware via IT management software is highly anomalous and malicious.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal endpoint management should never deliver or execute ransomware binaries.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Endpoint management tools may deploy legitimate software updates or scripts, but never ransomware.
key_indicators: File encryption and ransom note display
Execution initiated by remote management software

attack_chain.action: Attacker exploits pre-auth RCE vulnerability in Kaseya VSA server to gain code execution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to execute arbitrary commands on VSA server and managed endpoints.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses VSA server functionality to deploy ransomware payload to all managed endpoints.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ransomware executes on endpoints, encrypting files and demanding ransom.

behavioral_signatures: Unusual command execution on Kaseya VSA server without authentication
Mass deployment of binaries to endpoints via remote management tool
Simultaneous file encryption and ransom note creation across multiple endpoints
file_indicators: Unexpected executable files delivered via Kaseya VSA agent
Ransom note files (e.g., README.txt, ransom.txt) appearing on endpoints
network_indicators: Unusual outbound connections from Kaseya VSA server to attacker-controlled infrastructure
Spike in network traffic from VSA server to all managed endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for pre-authentication access and command execution attempts on Kaseya VSA endpoints. Alert on mass deployment of new executables or scripts to managed endpoints, especially if followed by file encryption activity. Look for creation of ransom note files and unusual outbound network connections from VSA servers or endpoints.
